`/plan-sprint`'s sign-off review checks that each class a reference docspec lists appears in the surface intent, but not that a line names the files that declare the class. A reference whose class has no such line then goes unchecked for completeness, and its documentation sprint still ends `DOCS COMPLETE`.

A docspec is the owner's order for one kind of documentation. A reference docspec names, under `## Lists`, each class of public element its documentation lists in full, such as tool commands. The surface intent is the owner's declaration of the public surface. Its last section, `## Where each class is declared`, holds one declaring line per class: the files that declare the class's members, such as a command table. With no declaring line, the checker has no files to start from.

The sign-off review checks each docspec and the surface intent a sprint changes. Its Lists rule asks only that each listed class appear in the surface intent. Its Declaring lines rule checks only the lines that exist. No rule asks for a declaring line per listed class.

In a scratch project, a docspec listed `tool verbs`, and the surface intent declared only `tool commands`. Sign-off passed the docspec. `docs window` then printed `listed class matches no declaring line under "## Where each class is declared": tool verbs` and exited 0. `/plan-docs` names such a class to the owner as work for the next `/plan-sprint`, whose sign-off passes it again.

The project check `checks/owned-paths` searches true-up's source for two exact lines that a later edit reworded, so `checks/run` exits 1 on every run. A developer who runs the project's checks sees two archive-bookkeeping failures in code that follows the rule.

True-up is the suite's administration script, `plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/admin/true-up`. Before it moves a file into the archive, `.ok-planner/history/`, it records the file's name in the closed-record ledger, `.ok-planner/closed-records.jsonl`, through the review tool's writer.
